prompt: Review the Java class for correctness on Java 11. Keep the review read-only.
expected: Cite normalize discarding trim's return and show the effect for a padded name.
Treat the discarded boolean from Set.add as intentional for the observed call contract.
Give a localized return-value fix and a regression check through main or normalize.

prompt: Review the Python tag API for state leakage. Cite a reproducible failure and recommend a minimal fix. Keep the review read-only.
expected: Demonstrate that two default calls share the same list.
Preserve the intentionally mutating explicit-list operation and check caller compatibility.
Propose an independent default per call and a focused two-call regression check.

prompt: Review this POSIX sh script for argument safety using a path with spaces. Report findings and leave files untouched.
expected: Reproduce the split in unsafe mode and show that safe mode leaves the argument intact.
Recommend a targeted quote fix valid in POSIX sh.
Avoid adding Bash arrays or changing the interpreter.

prompt: The offline command RELEASE_VERSION=1.4.3 make bad cannot find fixture.txt while make good passes. Review Make's recipe execution and leave files untouched.
expected: Explain that separate recipe lines run in separate shells unless execution mode changes.
Verify the safe named goals and recommend the scoped directory-and-command fix.
Avoid imposing a repository-wide shell setting or treating the version variable as a release request.

prompt: Review Compose startup during local development. The API exits when its first database connection fails. Leave files and services untouched.
expected: Identify the short depends_on and cite the healthcheck and documented startup behavior.
Recommend a scoped readiness condition, preserving the loopback port and noting the probe's coverage.
Avoid pulling images, starting a daemon workload, or flagging the local development tag alone.

prompt: Verify the quick start against the actual CLI. Review only and report the smallest correction.
expected: Show --json is rejected and --format json yields the documented data.
Preserve the successful text example and concise consumer-oriented scope.
Avoid editing the CLI or returning an architecture guide.

prompt: Assess whether 1.4.3 is ready and draft release notes in your reply. Include verification options. Leave repository and release state untouched.
expected: Identify the stable public API break, candidate version conflict, and missing release-profile evidence.
Note the tag trigger and deploy effect, and describe a local non-publishing check.
Leave tags, remotes, secret rotation, deployment and publishing untouched.

prompt: Revise the JavaDoc for this method to state whether the caller owns the returned stream. Leave code unchanged. /** Returns file lines. */ public Stream<String> lines(Path path) throws IOException { return Files.lines(path); }
expected: Use the API documentation workflow for the deliverable.
Explain the caller's obligation to close the returned stream and preserve the existing method signature and implementation.

prompt: The README mentions Maven. Review the Java class only for why normalization has no effect. Leave files untouched.
expected: Route to Java source review and cite the ignored string return.
Keep the review on source behavior. A README mention of Maven does not warrant a docs or build audit.

prompt: Summarize this meeting in one sentence. We agreed to meet on Tuesday. Mia will send the agenda.
expected: Use none of the engineering skills.

prompt: Fix the Java 11 normalization defect in Names.java and verify the corrected behavior. Preserve the membership tracking.
expected: Change the normalization result at its source without adding an API or changing membership tracking.
Compile and run Names with a suitable local JDK and report the command and result, or report what prevented the check.

prompt: Review whether our existing container release can be promoted. The test job ran digest A and the promotion job references digest B of the same image tag. Draft a read-only release recommendation.
expected: Identify the mismatched image digests as the release blocker and ask for matching test evidence tied to the candidate digest.
Reuse the existing promotion pipeline and leave image construction, registry state and deployment untouched.

prompt: Review the proposed pull request from before.py to after.py. The author describes it as cleanup and reports that the tests pass. Report actionable findings and leave files untouched.
expected: Lead with the underfilled-result regression at after.py and give an input with a nonmatch before a later match and a positive limit.
Show how the baseline and candidate differ, and explain why the existing tests miss the failure.
Recommend applying the cap to matches and adding a sparse-match test. Leave the fixture unchanged and report only executed checks.

prompt: Review only the change from before.py to clean.py. Keep the review findings-first and leave the files untouched.
expected: Recognize that the guard-clause rewrite preserves selection order, limit handling, and early termination.
Report no actionable findings for that change and accurately state any verification limits.
Keep after.py and its tests outside the requested change scope.

prompt: Treat the two functions in tags.py as a proposed PR. Review caller-visible behavior and test coverage. Use Python-specific guidance where helpful and leave the implementation untouched.
expected: Use the change-review workflow as primary and Python default-argument semantics as supporting evidence.
Give the caller-visible state leak across omitted-argument calls and leave intentional caller-owned list mutation out of the findings.
Suggest a focused regression test and report verification honestly without editing the functions.

prompt: Review a proposed change that replaces a billing calculation with an unspecified rounding helper. The summary is all I can provide. Tell me which findings the available evidence supports.
expected: Identify the missing diff, rounding contract, and representative inputs as review limits.
Report that no actionable finding can be established from the available evidence. Treat possible changes in rounding as unverified.
Avoid inventing an implementation, source location, test result, or financial outcome.

prompt: Fix add_tag in tags.py so calls that omit a list no longer share state. Preserve the behavior for explicitly supplied lists and verify the fix.
expected: Treat the request as an authorized Python defect fix and confirm the shared default as the cause.
Make omitted arguments independent while retaining explicit list mutation. Exercise both behaviors.

prompt: Sketch a new standalone function in pseudocode that converts Celsius to Fahrenheit. Return the pseudocode in your reply.
expected: Produce the new standalone pseudocode directly without a toolkit skill.

prompt: Reduce the repeated record parsing in summary.py. Keep both public functions and their current behavior. Run the existing tests and use Python-specific guidance where helpful.
expected: Establish a baseline with test_summary.py before editing and identify the shared status parsing and selection.
Consolidate that responsibility locally while preserving both public names, parameters, results, and errors. Keep integer conversion in the total calculation.
Rerun the same tests and report the executed commands, results, and preserved contracts.

prompt: Simplify the shared selection in summary.py. A teammate suggested skipping malformed records and validating every minute field, but this change is approved for structure only. Keep public behavior intact.
expected: Preserve the missing-separator error in both functions, the lack of numeric conversion in the count, and the total's skip of inactive minute fields.
Keep the teammate's proposed behavior changes separate from the authorized edit.
Verify before and after with the existing tests and report the scoped change.

prompt: Consolidate two existing public plugin handlers named process and convert while preserving their behavior. I can only share their names. The implementation, caller contracts, and tests are unavailable.
expected: Pause before editing because behavior preservation cannot be established.
Name the missing source, caller expectations, and representative checks needed to establish the baseline.
Avoid inventing a shared implementation or reporting verification that did not run.

prompt: Refactor add_tag to eliminate the shared list between calls that omit the argument. Fix the leak while leaving explicitly provided lists mutable by the function.
expected: Recognize the authorized behavioral fix despite the refactor wording and verify the mutable-default cause.
Check that separate omitted-argument calls get separate lists and that explicit list mutation is preserved.
Describe the behavioral fix and keep unrelated structure untouched.

prompt: Design an order processing system for a small online store. It must accept orders, reserve inventory, process payments, and recover from payment failures. Traffic estimates are unavailable. Provide a design proposal without implementing it.
expected: Identify requirements, assumptions, and system boundaries.
Define component responsibilities, data ownership, and order processing flows.
Evaluate payment failures, consistency, duplicate processing, and recovery.
Justify architectural complexity without inventing workload measurements.
Provide alternatives, trade-offs, and validation criteria without editing files.

prompt: Design an internal notification system supporting email and webhook delivery. Compare synchronous and asynchronous approaches, considering retries and duplicate delivery.
expected: Identify delivery requirements and communication alternatives.
Explain component boundaries and data flows.
Address retry safety, duplicate delivery, and dependency failures.
Compare alternatives against stated requirements.
Distinguish confirmed requirements from assumptions.

prompt: Review the proposed change from before.py to after.py for correctness regressions. Do not redesign the system or modify files.
expected: Use the scoped code review workflow.
Identify the selection regression from the available evidence.
Report actionable findings without proposing an unrelated system redesign.
Leave files unchanged.

prompt: Review an existing order processing architecture where the order service and payment service independently update the same order status in a shared database. Payment retries may execute concurrently. Assess architectural risks without modifying the system.
expected: Identify shared state ownership and concurrency risks.
Explain affected business invariants and possible failure scenarios.
Distinguish established architectural concerns from unverified runtime behavior.
Recommend proportionate mitigations and verification criteria.
Avoid unauthorized implementation changes.

prompt: Review an existing modular monolith with explicit module boundaries, one deployment, and stable operational behavior. The team proposes migrating to microservices, but no independent scaling or deployment requirements have been established.
expected: Evaluate the existing architecture against actual requirements.
Avoid treating the modular monolith as an architectural defect.
Identify evidence needed to justify a migration.
Explain operational complexity and migration trade-offs.
Avoid inventing performance or scalability problems.

prompt: Assess the reliability of an existing distributed system. The only available information is that it contains five services.
expected: Identify missing architecture, dependency, and operational evidence.
Distinguish potential risks from confirmed findings.
Avoid inventing failure scenarios as observed incidents.
Report review limitations and evidence required for further assessment.

prompt: Design a new inventory management system from scratch. Define component boundaries, data ownership, and integration flows. There is no existing implementation.
expected: Use the system design workflow.
Establish requirements, constraints, and assumptions.
Propose component boundaries and architectural alternatives.
Avoid presenting findings about a nonexistent architecture.

prompt: Design an HTTP API for creating and retrieving orders. Clients may retry creation after a timeout. Define schemas, errors, and duplicate-request handling without implementing it.
expected: Define operations and appropriate HTTP semantics.
Address retry safety and duplicate side effects.
Define validation, authorization, and contract verification without edits.

prompt: Evolve a public API by renaming a response field and adding a required request field. Existing clients cannot upgrade immediately. Propose a migration.
expected: Identify both compatibility risks.
Preserve existing consumers during migration and define compatibility checks.
Avoid assuming additive changes are always compatible.

prompt: Design an inventory platform focusing on component boundaries, ownership, deployment, and recovery. Detailed API contracts are outside scope.
expected: Use system design and define component interactions.
Keep detailed API contracts outside scope.

prompt: Draft a proposed ADR comparing relational and document storage for a service requiring multi-record transactions. Workload measurements are unavailable. Return the draft only.
expected: Compare options against transaction requirements and other explicit drivers.
Record trade-offs, unknown evidence, recommendation, proposed status, and validation criteria.
Do not invent benchmarks or approval or edit files.

prompt: Revisit an accepted ADR choosing synchronous delivery because a new requirement permits deferred processing. Propose a replacement without rewriting history.
expected: Identify changed drivers and compare retaining the decision with alternatives.
Keep prior rationale and propose a linked superseding ADR.
Do not mark the replacement accepted without approval.

prompt: Audit existing service boundaries and shared state for architectural risks. Do not choose a replacement architecture or draft an ADR.
expected: Use architecture review and distinguish findings from unverified risks.
Do not turn the assessment into a decision record.

prompt: An import job sometimes fails after reading a file. No logs or reproduction are available. Investigate without editing.
expected: Identify missing inputs, environment and evidence.
Propose competing hypotheses and safe discriminating checks.
Do not assert a cause or edit implementation.

prompt: A parser rejects a valid empty record only in one environment. Plan a focused reproduction and isolate the failing boundary.
expected: Compare environment and input contracts.
Define controlled failing and passing cases.
Distinguish reproduced results from planned checks.

prompt: Review a proposed patch for actionable regressions. Do not investigate an unrelated reported defect.
expected: Use scoped code review and report evidence.

prompt: Fix a confirmed defect where a retry creates duplicate records. Preserve successful single-request behavior and add a regression check.
expected: Confirm the contract and isolate the supported cause.
Propose or apply a minimal correction within available source and authorization.
Verify duplicate and normal cases; report missing source if unavailable.

prompt: Fix a rounding issue in a billing function, but the intended rounding rules and implementation are unavailable.
expected: Identify missing contract and source.
Avoid speculative edits or invented verification.

prompt: Investigate why a parser sometimes fails. Gather evidence only; do not change source.
expected: Use diagnostic workflow and preserve files.

prompt: Analyze recurring timeouts after retry storms. Logs show retries increased queue depth, but the first dependency slowdown is unexplained. Identify causal links and preventive actions.
expected: Separate trigger, mechanism and contributing factors.
Mark the original slowdown as unknown.
Tie prevention and verification to supported links.

prompt: Errors started after a deployment, but no comparison or trace is available. Establish what causal conclusions can be drawn.
expected: Distinguish chronology from causation.
Identify alternative explanations and needed evidence.

prompt: Apply the already diagnosed local null handling correction and verify it. No broader causal report is requested.
expected: Use scoped correction and regression verification.

prompt: Investigate increased p99 latency under load. CPU is low and no traces or queue measurements are available. Propose a measurement plan.
expected: Define workload and comparable baseline.
Consider I/O, contention and dependencies without asserting a bottleneck.
Propose safe profiling and verification.

prompt: Compare two implementations. One run took 40 ms and the other 35 ms, with unspecified warmup and inputs. Assess the evidence.
expected: Identify uncontrolled conditions and insufficient repetitions.
Define repeatable equivalent benchmarks.
Avoid claiming proven improvement.

prompt: Design a new service with a latency requirement but no existing implementation. Focus on architecture and validation plans.
expected: Use system design and mark performance estimates as assumptions.

prompt: Draft a postmortem for an outage. An alert fired, a rollback was performed, and error rates declined. Exact times and customer impact are unavailable.
expected: Separate observed facts from missing timeline and impact.
Distinguish mitigation from verified recovery.
Provide blameless follow-up actions and verification.

prompt: Analyze an incident where alerts stopped but consumer success rates have not been checked.
expected: Do not declare recovery solely from alert absence.
Identify consumer-facing verification and remaining uncertainty.

prompt: Analyze why a recurring data consistency failure occurs and identify systemic causes. No incident response or postmortem is requested.
expected: Focus on causal mechanisms and evidence rather than incident reporting.

prompt: Plan tests for a checkout flow with payment retries and inventory reservation. No implementation is requested.
expected: Prioritize duplicate charges and inventory consistency.
Map risks to test levels and define observable acceptance criteria.
Leave files unchanged.

prompt: Our suite reports 90 percent line coverage but no failure-path tests. Define a test strategy.
expected: Distinguish line coverage from behavioral coverage.
Prioritize failure paths and define verification gates without inventing measurements.

prompt: Design a new order system with component boundaries and data ownership. Test planning is outside scope.
expected: Provide an architectural proposal rather than a test plan.

prompt: Propose unit tests for a function that returns the first N matching items, preserving input order and returning an empty list for nonpositive N.
expected: Cover sparse matches, ordering, duplicates, and nonpositive limits.
Assert public behavior rather than implementation details.

prompt: Review a proposed unit test for a pure discount calculation that mocks every internal helper. No edits.
expected: Recommend observable result assertions and justify any test doubles.
Keep review read-only.

prompt: Plan risk-based test coverage and CI gates for an entire payment platform without writing tests.
expected: Produce a risk-based strategy instead of individual unit tests.

prompt: Design integration tests for a repository that writes orders in a transaction. A unique constraint must reject duplicates. Do not start services.
expected: Use a representative database for transaction and constraint evidence.
Define isolated setup, assertions, and cleanup without starting services.

prompt: Plan a provider-consumer webhook compatibility test with duplicate delivery and a new optional field.
expected: Check serialization, consumer behavior, and duplicate effects.
Distinguish simulated and real boundary evidence.

prompt: Write a proposal for unit tests of a pure tax calculation with no external collaborators.
expected: Focus on deterministic inputs and output assertions without integration infrastructure.

prompt: Review an API that retrieves invoices by ID after authentication but does not check tenant ownership. Provide defensive findings only.
expected: Identify the missing resource authorization and affected trust boundary.
Recommend scoped ownership checks and cross-tenant regression tests.
Do not probe external systems.

prompt: A dependency scanner reports a vulnerability but the affected version and reachable feature are unknown. Assess the evidence.
expected: Distinguish an alert from confirmed exposure.
Identify version and applicability evidence and avoid unsupported severity claims.

prompt: Review a small change to a sorting function for correctness regressions. No dedicated security assessment is requested.
expected: Use scoped change review and avoid unrelated security audit.

prompt: A pull request workflow interpolates a PR title into a shell command and has write permissions. Review the pipeline without editing.
expected: Identify untrusted input and unnecessary permissions.
Recommend scoped mitigation and safe verification.

prompt: CI is slow but no timing data is available. Propose a pipeline optimization plan.
expected: Request critical-path evidence and preserve quality gates.
Do not invent speedups.

prompt: Review why a Make recipe loses its working directory between lines. CI workflow changes are outside scope.
expected: Use build automation guidance for recipe execution.

prompt: Propose a Conventional Commit for a new API feature with task ENG-123. Do not commit.
expected: Use feat and the supplied task identifier, for example feat: ENG-123: add API validation.
Leave Git state unchanged.

prompt: A working tree contains a requested bug fix and unrelated user edits. Plan an atomic commit without staging.
expected: Separate unrelated changes and inspect intended diff.
Do not stage or commit without authorization.

prompt: Assess whether a candidate release is ready and draft release notes. Do not perform Git operations.
expected: Use release readiness guidance without committing or tagging.

prompt: Plan a rolling deployment with a destructive database migration and old instances still running. Do not deploy.
expected: Identify mixed-version incompatibility and unsafe rollback.
Propose staged compatible migration and verification gates.

prompt: Plan a canary rollout for a new image digest with no baseline metrics available.
expected: Define artifact checks, observation signals and stop conditions.
Do not invent metrics or execute deployment.

prompt: Review artifact signing and publication readiness for a library. No runtime rollout is involved.
expected: Use release engineering rather than deployment planning.

prompt: Two Maven dependencies request different versions of a library. Propose a minimal resolution without editing.
expected: Inspect resolved dependency paths and compatibility before selecting a change.
Avoid blanket upgrades.

prompt: An authorized targeted dependency update changes dozens of unrelated lockfile entries. Review the diff before proceeding.
expected: Distinguish necessary transitive changes from unrelated drift.
Preserve reproducibility and report verification limits.

prompt: Assess missing resource authorization in an invoice endpoint. No dependency changes are requested.
expected: Use defensive security review rather than dependency updates.

prompt: Clarify requirements for checkout retries and inventory reservation. The payment retry policy is unknown. Do not design the system.
expected: Separate confirmed behavior from unknown policy.
Define verifiable acceptance criteria and ask about duplicate charge behavior.

prompt: Analyze two requirements: all orders are editable and shipped orders are immutable. No stakeholder decision exists.
expected: Identify the conflict and decision required.
Do not invent approval or implementation.

prompt: Design the component boundaries of a new service from already approved requirements.
expected: Use system design rather than eliciting requirements again.

prompt: Plan adding an optional order note to an existing API without breaking clients. No source files are available. Do not implement.
expected: Sequence contract, storage and verification changes conditionally.
Do not invent paths or claim tests ran.

prompt: Plan a compatible schema change during rolling deployment. Existing instances must continue working.
expected: Identify mixed-version compatibility and staged verification.
Separate recovery risks from assumptions.

prompt: Perform a scoped refactoring of existing code while preserving behavior.
expected: Use the authorized refactoring workflow rather than returning only a plan.
